newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel inmates surrender control of Colombian prison.
newsitem.headline: Rebel inmates surrender control of Colombian prison.

text.p: Rebel inmates laid down their weapons and surrendered control of a prison in northern Colombia on Monday, 11 days after staging a bloody riot in which three guards and a police officer were killed.
The surrender came just one day after heavily armed inmates freed the last 11 hostages being held inside the prison in Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province.

The release, and Monday's return of control over the facility to prison guards, were part of a negotiated settlement of the uprising that was brokered by members of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

In exchange, government officials agreed to take no reprisals against leaders of the uprising and to move quickly to improve conditions inside the prison, which was built to house no more than 150 inmates but currently holds more than 580.

Police and penal authorities said the 47 weapons handed over by inmates included a submachine gun, 21 rifles, five shotguns and 19 revolvers. They had been seized from guards, and from a prison storage area, when the riot erupted on April 3.
In all, 16 hostages were taken at the start of the uprising. All were released unharmed.

Leaders of the riot originally demanded helicopters and bulletproof vests for a ride to freedom and possible exile in Cuba. They settled for the promise of improved living conditions, a change of the prison's guards, and a pledge that some of their cases would be reviewed by a special judge.
